Complete this **5–10-minute access check before Day 1**, if possible. No software
installation, new model fitting or R/GLM knowledge is required. The course is about
Bayesian thinking, ecological interpretation, uncertainty and checking models.
The materials are in English. Tell the instructor if you need help reading them.

## Everyone: check the reading copies (about 5 minutes)

1. Download and unzip the participant archive. Keep its folder structure.
2. Open `day1/exercise-student.html` and `day1/results.html` locally. Check that
   figures, equations and tables appear. Repeat for Days 2 and 3.
3. Disconnect the network and check that these HTMLs still open. This is a complete
   route through the core comparison and interpretation questions.
4. Tell the instructor if any reading copy fails. Course times are 19:00–20:30
   China time (UTC+8), 21–23 October 2026. No homework is required.

## Optional: check the prepared browser R environment (about 5 minutes)

If you want to run the supplied code, open your assigned RStudio URL, log in and
open `afec-bayes-2026.Rproj`. Run the following completed code. The instructor can
help with the editor; writing R code independently is not required.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(posterior)
library(here)
source(here("R/course_utils.R"))
fit <- fit_or_load("day1_seedling", "stan/binomial.stan",
                  list(N = 5, y = 2, a = 1, b = 1), use_precomputed = TRUE)
fit$source
nrow(fit$draws)
mean(fit$draws$p)
plot_update(2, 5)
```

Expected: `precomputed`, 4000 draws, mean near 0.43, and a plot. This reads a
supplied fit; it does not compile or sample. Save a short note, log out and back
in, and check that the note remains. Report errors without sharing your password.

If this does not work, use the HTML reading copies. Do not install software or
restore renv during class. Work individually, with nearby discussion if useful.
Predict before looking at each result, then explain the comparison in words.

[Packages and optional local setup](PACKAGES.md) lists the small package set for
running the core code. brms, cmdstanr, CmdStan and a C++ toolchain are only for
optional demonstrations or later exploration; no student inference preflight is
required. The instructor checks any fitting demonstration separately before class.
